name: Google Cloud Storage
description: Protects against destructive GCS operations like bucket removal, \ object deletion, and recursive deletes.

destructive_patterns.name: gsutil-rb
destructive_patterns.description: gsutil rb removes a GCS bucket.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a GCS bucket deletes the bucket and potentially all objects within it. \ Bucket names are globally unique and may not be immediately available for reuse. \ Applications and services referencing this bucket will fail.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gsutil ls gs://bucket: List bucket contents first \ - gsutil -m cp -r gs://bucket ./backup: Backup contents locally \ - Enable object versioning before testing deletions

destructive_patterns.name: gsutil-rm
destructive_patterns.description: gsutil rm deletes objects from GCS.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting GCS objects permanently removes data unless versioning is enabled. \ With -r flag, entire directory trees are deleted recursively. Without \ versioning, deleted objects cannot be recovered.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gsutil ls: Preview what will be deleted \ - Enable bucket versioning for recovery options \ - gsutil mv: Move to archive bucket instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: gsutil-rsync-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gsutil rsync -d deletes destination objects not in source.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The -d flag with gsutil rsync deletes destination objects that don't exist \ in the source. If source and destination are swapped, or source is empty, \ this can result in total data loss at the destination.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gsutil rsync -n -d: Dry run to preview deletions \ - gsutil rsync without -d: Only adds/updates, never deletes \ - Backup destination before syncing

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-storage-buckets-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud storage buckets delete removes a GCS bucket.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a GCS bucket removes the bucket configuration and all objects within it \ (if --recursive is used). The globally unique bucket name may not be immediately \ reclaimable. All dependent applications will fail.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud storage buckets describe: Review bucket configuration \ - gcloud storage cp -r: Backup contents before deletion \ - Remove objects first to understand data being deleted

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-storage-objects-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud storage objects delete removes objects from GCS.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting GCS objects permanently removes data. Without object versioning, \ deleted files cannot be recovered. Production data should be backed up \ before deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud storage objects describe: Verify object before deletion \ - Enable bucket versioning for soft deletes \ - Move to archive storage class instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-storage-rm
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud storage rm removes objects from GCS.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The rm command deletes objects and can recursively remove entire bucket \ contents. Deleted objects are permanently lost unless versioning is enabled. \ Wildcards can unexpectedly match more files than intended.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud storage ls: Preview files matching pattern \ - Enable bucket versioning before testing \ - gcloud storage mv: Move to archive bucket instead
